column2: M120 site declaration — every data-raw harness that RESUMES from a checkpoint.
A site here reads a cache back and may therefore serve rows the current design
never computed; harnesses that only WRITE a checkpoint are deliberately absent
(they cannot serve a stale row). This file is the declared enumeration AC4
quantifies over — it is not, and never claims to be, a discovery procedure over
all harnesses. That job belongs to the run-time trace in checkpoint-guard.R,
which observes deserializations rather than spellings.
script       path relative to the repo root
params       the design parameters compared on resume, in the declared order;
the mismatch message names the EARLIEST differing one in this order
roots        the site's ENTRY POINTS into its own generating code. The hashed
block is the call closure of these — every function they reach
that the site itself defines — so a helper added later is covered
without anyone remembering to list it. Package functions stop the
walk: their behavior is pinned by the test suite, not by this hash
values       the non-function determinants, which are declared rather than
derived: seed-offset vectors, sampler argument lists, and the
formula and prior each base fit is compiled from. Following data
references instead would drag in the compiled model object itself
exemptions   determinants the walk reaches but cannot hash, each with its reason
below. Empty on a site with none. This list WEAKENS the check, so
it is the one place a determinant may go uncovered, and it is a
recorded decision rather than a silent omission.
base_fit — a compiled brms/Stan fit; not stably deparsable, and
what determines it (base_formula, base_prior, brm_args) is hashed.
unit         what one checkpoint entry covers
api          the guard calls the site must make — ALL of them, live. A site
that keeps its file-level call and drops its per-entry one has
stopped checking the thing that goes stale, so no single call
stands in for the set
